identity.name: Bar Kokhba State
alt_names: Jewish state of the Bar Kokhba revolt

land.text: the province of Judaea, of which the rebels held 'all of Judea proper'

predecessors.note: The roman-empire dossier carries the matching contest 132-135 (counterpart 'Jewish rebels of Judaea').

land.text: Judaea, which Hadrian merged with Galilee and Samaria 'into the new province of Syria Palaestina' (Simon bar Kokhba page)

successors.note: The Bar Kokhba revolt page does not mention the renaming; the Simon bar Kokhba page does, undated.

capitals.name: Betar (Battir)
capitals.note: 'Betar was chosen as the rebels' headquarters'; Herodium was 'a regional headquarters and wheat store'. The Simon bar Kokhba page names no capital and says only that he 'took refuge in the fortress of Betar during the final phase'. The page gives no coordinates; those are the village of Battir.

rulers.name: Simon bar Kokhba
rulers.title: nasi (prince) of Israel
rulers.note: Infobox reign 132-135; he 'crowned himself as nasi'; killed by Roman troops at Betar in 135.

correction.text: 'all of Judea proper (not the entire province of Judaea)'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Most scholars agree the rebels held all of Judea proper (not the entire province of Judaea)'; coinage shows rebel presence in most areas 'into the third year of the uprising'. Whether they held Jerusalem is disputed (the Israel Antiquities Authority argues they never captured it, citing only four Bar Kokhba coins found there as of 2020). The gazetteer's Judea region (9 thousand km2) is the Judean hills; the Galilee and Samaria were not held. No area on either page.

region.text: 'all of Judea proper (not the entire province of Judaea)'

ledger.note: 132: the Bar Kokhba revolt founds a Jewish state. The revolt 'likely erupted in the summer of 132 CE' and by then the rebels had set up an independent state; silver tetradrachms from the first year carry 'Year One of the Redemption of Israel'; Simon bar Kokhba 'crowned himself as nasi' (prince) of Israel. The page gives no month for the state's founding.

region.text: 'all of Judea proper (not the entire province of Judaea)'

ledger.note: 135: Betar falls and the state ends. Betar was besieged in summer 135 and 'captured and destroyed in 135 CE'; Bar Kokhba was killed there (Simon bar Kokhba page: 'Roman troops killed him at Betar ... in 135'). Zissu has the conflict persisting 'at least until January 136' and Eck 'early 136' by Hadrian's imperator acclamation; Jews were expelled from Jerusalem and the surrounding district.

wars.name: Bar Kokhba revolt

zones.text: 'all of Judea proper (not the entire province of Judaea)'

wars.outcome: Roman victory: Betar was besieged in summer 135 and captured and destroyed; Bar Kokhba was killed; the conflict persisted 'at least until January 136' (Zissu) or ended 'in early 136' (Eck); Jews were expelled from Jerusalem and its district.
wars.note: Hadrian appointed Sextus Julius Severus, transferred from Britannia (no date); Tineius Rufus is the governor of Judaea in Eusebius (no date); Hadrian had visited Judaea in 129-130 and later joined the campaign for a time. [Reviewer eu-04-x, 2026-10-19: war end cut from 136 to 135 to keep the war inside the state's life (dissolve at the fall of Betar, 135); the page's 'at least until January 136' and 'early 136' remain the end of the fighting, not of the state.]

certainty.note: The held territory is a scholars' reading of coinage and letters, not a boundary.

sources.title: Bar Kokhba revolt
sources.note: Outbreak summer 132, the independent state and coinage, territory held, Betar 135, end 135/136.

sources.title: Simon bar Kokhba
sources.note: Nasi title, the state of about three years, death at Betar 135, the merged province Syria Palaestina.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, named by the roman-empire dossier ('Jewish rebels of Judaea', contest 132-135). Two pages opened. The Judea Cliopatria row ends in 5 and the judea dossier in 6, so there is no Jewish state to be the predecessor; the province of Judaea is. The extent is 'all of Judea proper' and nothing more precise on the pages (no toparchies, no Jerusalem). The first-revolt provisional government (66-70) is the dossier jewish-provisional-government. Wikidata id unknown.
